shots.title: The Live tab: the whole window

callouts.what: the band across the very top, which says whether the system as a whole is well: whether it is recording, whether pictures are arriving, whether anything is watching them, and how the radio link is
the row of tabs that chooses which page is shown; the page you are on is the one with the amber bar under its name
the name of what this camera watches, written in Hebrew above the pictures
the buttons that choose which picture fills the wall: all of them side by side, or one of them on its own
the button that puts the pictures on the whole screen
the plate above each picture, giving the name of that camera view and what it is doing right now
one of the two live pictures; dragging near its edge steers the camera, and so do the arrow keys
the zoom bar belonging to that picture; there is one for each lens
the Link panel, which says in one word how the radio link between the camera and this laptop is doing
the Storage panel: how much of the allowed space the recordings have used, and how long before the oldest starts being deleted
the Movement line, which counts what has moved today and says when the last one was

shots.title: The column of readings beside the pictures

callouts.what: what the camera head is doing right now: idle, or the speed it is being driven at
the keys that steer the camera, written out
the one word for the state of the radio link: GOOD, FAIR, BUSY, FULL, WEAK or NO LINK
the two bars under it: how strong the signal is, and how much of the link is being used, each with the point where it stops being healthy marked on the track
how much space the recordings have used out of what they are allowed, and how long there is before the oldest is deleted
the movements counted today; pressing this line opens the footage of the newest one, when the Playback tab is switched on

shots.title: Choosing which picture is shown

callouts.what: the name of what this camera watches, in Hebrew
the button that shows every camera view side by side; it is the one that is on here, marked by the amber bar beneath it
a button that gives one camera view the whole wall on its own; there is one for each view the camera has
the button into fullscreen, where only the pictures are left

shots.title: The zoom bar under a picture

callouts.what: the minus button, which zooms this lens out to a wider view
the handle, which sits where the camera says the lens actually is; dragging it sends the lens somewhere
the plus button, which zooms this lens in closer
the reading: the word zoom and how far in the lens is, as the camera itself reported it and never as a guess
the bottom of the picture this bar belongs to; the bar sits inside that picture's own frame, and the other picture has one of its own

shots.title: The status band with nothing wrong

callouts.what: the recording dot: a red circle that pulses while footage is reaching the disk, and a still red bar when it is not
each part of the system in turn - recording, pictures, movement watching, the radio link - named on its own while there is nothing wrong with it, and spelled out in full the moment there is
the radio link between the camera and this laptop; the figures behind it are in the Link panel on the Live tab

shots.title: The status band with something wrong

callouts.what: the recording dot: a red circle that pulses while footage is reaching the disk, and a still red bar when it is not
each part of the system in turn - recording, pictures, movement watching, the radio link - named on its own while there is nothing wrong with it, and spelled out in full the moment there is
the radio link between the camera and this laptop; the figures behind it are in the Link panel on the Live tab

shots.title: The Live tab with an alarm up

callouts.what: the red strip that appears under the pictures when something has moved, saying which camera saw it and at what time
the red outline drawn round the picture the movement was seen on
the button that clears the strip and the red outline once the movement has been seen
the same movement counted in the column beside the pictures, where it stays after the strip has been cleared

shots.title: The alarm strip, close up

callouts.what: the filled bar drawn beside the words, so that the alarm is not carried by the colour alone
which camera view the movement was seen on, and the time it happened
the button that takes the strip down again

shots.title: Fullscreen: only the pictures

callouts.what: the name of what this camera watches, still on the screen in fullscreen: it is what says which of the two consoles this is
the way back out, which names its own key; Esc and F11 do the same
the view buttons, which are kept in fullscreen
the zoom bars, which are kept in fullscreen too

shots.title: Settings: the camera itself

callouts.what: the name of what this camera watches, in your own words; it is written above the pictures and on the window itself
which monitor this console opens on, so that the two consoles do not land on top of each other after a restart
the camera's address on the network
the username the camera expects
the camera's password, shown as it was typed and never hidden behind dots, so that a mistyped one can be seen and corrected

shots.title: Settings: the camera's views

callouts.what: the name of one camera view; it is the name this view goes by everywhere else in the console
the address the camera serves that view on
the tick that watches this view for movement; it is ticked here, so this view is being watched
the same tick on the other view, unticked: no view is watched for movement until it is asked for
the button that shows a picture from this view so that parts of it can be drawn round and ignored
a fold holding the one setting that makes a view more or less touchy; it is shut until it is needed
the button for when the zoom bar under one picture moves the other picture; it exchanges the two lenses

shots.title: Settings: movement detection and the alarm sound

callouts.what: the master switch: with it off nothing is watched for movement whatever the camera views say, and recording carries on either way
the switch for the sound an alarm makes as well as the red strip; it never sounds more than once every twelve seconds, and it can be turned off if somebody sleeps in the room

shots.title: Settings: switching the Playback tab on, and the question it asks

callouts.what: the tick that adds the Playback tab to the console; the tab is off normally, and this tick stays down until the question below it has been answered
the "Are you sure" pane the tick raises, which says what switching the tab on brings back with it
the button that agrees, which is what actually switches the tab on
the button that leaves it off and takes the question away

shots.title: Settings: where the recordings go and how much room they may take

callouts.what: the folder the recordings are written to
the button that looks at the drive and fills in a size and an age rule to match it; it changes the two boxes below and nothing else, and nothing is written until Save
how much of the drive the recordings are allowed to fill; the slider stops at the size of the drive
the same size as a number, which can be typed instead of dragged
what that size means in days of footage
the age rule: anything older than this many days is deleted whether there is room for it or not; empty means nothing is deleted because of its age
the line saying which of the two rules is the one actually deleting footage today

shots.title: Settings: the radio link

callouts.what: the radio's address; without it the Link panel on the Live tab has nothing to read
the radio's username
the radio's password, shown as typed like every other password here
the switch that lets the console ask the camera for a smaller picture by itself while the link is busy, and for a better one again once it has been quiet

shots.title: Settings: the tools for checking the camera

callouts.what: the fold holding the camera tools; it is shut until it is pressed, and nothing inside it changes a setting
the button that asks whether the camera is answering at all
the button that hunts for the camera's address when nobody knows it
the button that asks which lens is behind which picture
the button that asks the camera for a smaller picture, once, when the link cannot carry the one it is sending
the button that writes everything it found into a file that can be sent to somebody
the box the answers appear in

shots.title: Settings: saving, and what it says when it will not

callouts.what: the line that appears when a setting was refused, saying which one and why; nothing at all was saved while this is showing
the button that writes these settings to the file; nothing typed on this page takes effect until it is pressed, and Ctrl+S does the same

shots.title: The Logs tab

callouts.what: the button showing every line; it is the one that is on, marked by the amber bar under it
the button that hides everything except the warnings and the errors
the button that copies the lines being shown, so that they can be pasted somewhere and sent to somebody
a line in red, which is an error; this one is the camera refusing the username and password that are in Settings
the four columns: when the line was written, how serious it is, which part of the system said it, and what it said
the tick that keeps the table on the newest line as lines arrive; untick it to stay where you have scrolled to while you read

shots.title: The Playback tab, once it has been switched on

callouts.what: the day being looked at; the buttons either side of it step one day back and one day forward
which camera view is being looked back through
the clock: the moment the picture below it is showing
how much of the day the bar at the bottom covers: the whole of it, an hour, or ten minutes
the bar for the day: the filled green parts are what was recorded, and the gaps are the times nothing was
the marks on the bar where something moved; pressing one plays the footage of it
play and pause
how fast the footage is played back
the start of a piece of footage to keep; Mark end beside it is the other end of it
the button that writes the marked piece to a folder you choose

shots.title: Marking the parts of a picture to ignore

callouts.what: the instruction: drag around anything that should be ignored, and click a marked area to take it off again
an area already marked out, shaded in red over the picture; movement inside it is never reported
a second marked area, this one dragged as a box rather than drawn round
the tool that draws round a shape freehand; it is the one that is on, marked by the amber bar beneath it
the tool that drags a rectangle instead
the button that takes off the area drawn last
the button that takes off every marked area at once
the button that leaves the marked areas exactly as they were
the button that keeps what was drawn; Save on the Settings tab is what writes it to the file
